case.question: what is a signal transduction pathway example
case.expected_answer: Epinephrine signalling that triggers glucose release from liver cells, involving G-protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP and protein kinases.
case.support_quote: Epinephrine is used as a sample messenger to trigger the release of glucose from cells in the liver. The G-Protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinases are all used as illustrative examples of signal transduction.
case.source_qualification: An illustrative pathway named in the supplied teaching-video description; no additional intermediate steps are inferred.
family_reference_texts: 038 - Signal Transduction Pathways.mov Paul Andersen explains how signal transduction pathways are used by cells to convert chemical messages to cellular action. Epinephrine is used as a sample messenger to trigger the release of glucose from cells in the liver. The G-Protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinases are all used as illustrative examples of signal transduction.

passages.text: An overview of major signal transduction pathways in mammals. Signal transduction refers to the transmission of a molecular signal in the form of a chemical modification by recruitment of protein complexes along a pathway that ultimately triggers a biochemical event in the cell.

Signal transduction occurs when an extracellular signaling molecule activates a specific receptor located on the cell surface or inside the cell. In turn, this receptor triggers a biochemical chain of events inside the cell, creating a response.

Signal transduction occurs when an extracellular signaling molecule activates a specific receptor located on the cell surface or inside the cell. In turn, this receptor triggers a biochemical chain of events inside the cell – known as a signaling cascade – that eventually elicits a response.
Signal transduction: A basic process in molecular cell biology involving the conversion of a signal from outside the cell to a functional change within the cell.

The signal transduction pathway is the mechanism by which the energy of a photon signals a mechanism in the cell that leads to its electrical polarization. 1  This polarization ultimately leads to either the transmittance or inhibition of a neural signal that will be fed to the brain via the optic nerve.
